column2: The upstream mod id quoted in evidence/m6/review.md as the injected identifier in two mutation-test refusal logs. This historical evidence records what the boundary check rejected, not a Ravel public API or implementation.
An ordinary English past participle, used throughout the loader and the SDK about configuration. The collision is with a mod id that took the same word.
An ordinary English verb, used throughout the loader and the SDK about creating values, sessions and directories. The pinned pack contains a mod whose id took the same word.

The name of the pack script tree SPEC.md and ROADMAP.md describe as ATM-authored material Ravel must not transcribe. Naming the tree is what those sentences are for; the word is the tree, and the mod id it collides with is the tree's implementation upstream.
An ordinary English adjective, used in SPEC.md and the observability crate about what Ravel exposes. The collision is with a mod id that took the same word.
An ordinary English verb in a conformance-test comment about declaration sets becoming smaller. The pinned pack contains a mod whose id took the same word.

Ravel's own M4 test mod, test-mods/waystone-ledger/, written in M4 and so predating this workspace. It is named for the generic modding concept and for the conventional c:waystones tag any mod may declare, not for the pinned entry that shares the word.
